A3-countershading

Three animals in one horizontal row, each clearly separated with white space, each with a soft pale yellow band of light shining down from above it: 1) a fish swimming to the left, side view, dark grey-blue on the back fading smoothly to silvery-white on the belly; 2) a toad sitting on a little soil, side view, olive-brown mottled back with a pale cream belly visible at the side; 3) a snake partly coiled on the ground, with a darker patterned back and a paler plain belly visible on its curled side. Soft natural colours.
A3-warning-colouration

A small forest-floor scene on a patch of leaf litter: a fly agaric mushroom with a bright red cap covered in white warty spots and a white stalk with a ring; beside it a smaller bright orange mushroom; and a little apart from them, for contrast, a dull plain brown mushroom. White background around the scene.
A3-termite-castes

Five kinds of termite in one horizontal row, at their relative sizes, with white space between them: 1) a huge queen with a very swollen, pale, sausage-shaped abdomen and a small dark head and thorax at one end; 2) a normal-sized dark brown king; 3) a small pale soft-bodied worker; 4) a soldier with a large dark orange-brown head and long curved jaws; 5) a dark-brown winged reproductive (alate) with two pairs of long equal wings lying flat over its body. All seen from above. Soft creams and browns.
A3-termite-mound

A cut-away view of a tall savanna termite mound standing on red soil, cut in half from top to bottom to show the inside. The thick hard outer clay wall with thin air channels and chimneys running up through it to openings at the top. A central royal chamber near ground level containing a large pale queen with a swollen abdomen. Several chambers around it holding pale honeycomb-like fungus gardens. A few nursery chambers with tiny white eggs and young. Tunnels leading out underground into the red soil. Warm reddish-browns and creams.
A3-agama-basking

Two panels side by side, clearly separated. Left: an Agama lizard basking on a flat sunlit rock in the morning, with its body flattened against the rock and its side turned towards a low sun in the top left corner; warm sunlight. Right: the same lizard at midday resting in cool shade under an overhanging rock, with a high sun at the top. Warm oranges, browns and blues.
A3-aestivation

Two panels side by side, clearly separated. Left: a cut-away of the dried, cracked mud bottom of a dried-up pond, with an African lungfish (long eel-like fish with thin thread-like fins) curled up inside a hardened mucus cocoon buried in the mud, and a small breathing tube leading up to the surface. Right: a land snail with its shell opening sealed by a thin whitish dried mucus membrane, partly buried in dry soil. Soft browns and greys.
A3-bird-beaks

Eight bird heads in profile facing left, arranged in a neat 4 by 2 grid with generous white space between them (no frames): top row: a weaver bird with a short thick cone-shaped beak; an eagle with a strong hooked beak; a sunbird with a long thin curved beak; a duck with a broad flat beak. Bottom row: a kingfisher with a long straight dagger-like beak; a woodpecker with a strong straight chisel-like beak; a domestic hen with a short pointed beak; a parrot with a large curved hooked beak. Soft natural colours.
A3-bird-feet

Six bird feet arranged in a neat 3 by 2 grid with generous white space between them (no frames): top row: a perching foot with three toes forward and one back gripping a thin twig; a raptor foot with long curved sharp talons gripping a branch; a webbed duck foot. Bottom row: a long thin wading leg with long spread toes standing in shallow water; a sturdy scratching foot of a hen with blunt claws on soil; a climbing foot with two toes forward and two toes back gripping vertical tree bark. Soft natural colours.
A3-insect-mouthparts

Three insect heads in side view, each in its own column with white space between: 1) a female mosquito head with its long proboscis piercing a patch of skin: the outer sheath (labium) bent back in an elbow shape while a bundle of fine needle-like stylets goes into the skin; 2) a butterfly head with a long proboscis coiled up like a watch spring under the head, and a clubbed antenna; 3) a moth head with its long straight proboscis uncoiled and reaching deep into a tubular flower, and a feathery antenna. Soft natural colours.
A3-camouflage-defence

Three panels in one row, each clearly separated: 1) a stick insect on a brown twig, its long thin brown body and legs looking just like the twig; 2) a green praying mantis on a leafy stem with its spiny front legs folded together under its head as if praying; 3) a warty brown toad on soil and dead leaves, puffed up, with a large oval parotid gland bulge behind its eye. Soft greens and browns.
A3-agama-display

A male and a female Agama lizard on a plain sunlit wall. The male is larger, perched high on the top of the wall, with a bright orange-red head and front part of the tail, a dark blue-black body, raised up on his straightened front legs with his head lifted in a head-bobbing display. The female is smaller and lower down on the wall, brown with pale spots and an orange patch on her side. Warm oranges, blues and browns.
A3-bird-courtship

Two scenes side by side, clearly separated. Left: a peacock with its long tail fanned out in a full upright semicircle of shimmering green and blue eyespot feathers, facing a plain brown peahen. Right: a bright yellow male village weaver bird with a black face hanging upside down from the bottom of a round woven grass nest and flapping its wings, the nest hanging from a palm frond. Soft natural colours.
A3-skin-section

A vertical cross-section block of mammalian skin, shown as a rectangular slice. Top: the thin outer epidermis with a flat surface. Below: the thick dermis containing one hair growing out of a hair follicle, a small erector (arrector pili) muscle attached to the follicle at an angle, a small sebaceous gland beside the follicle, a coiled sweat gland deep in the dermis with a long duct running up to open as a pore on the surface, red and blue capillaries and small blood vessels near the top, and a few nerve fibres with nerve endings. Bottom: a thick layer of round yellow fat cells (subcutaneous fat). Soft pinks, creams and yellows.
A3-cactus-pangolin

Two organisms side by side, clearly separated. Left: a prickly pear cactus with thick, flat, green fleshy pads and small clusters of sharp spines instead of leaves, growing in dry sandy soil. Right: a pangolin covered in large, overlapping brown scales, walking on dry ground, side view facing right, with its long tail. Soft greens, browns and sand colours.
